overview: Two membrane-bound organelles that both handle breakdown reactions, but with very different enzymes and targets.
genZNote: Lysosome: the cell's demolition crew. Peroxisome: the cell's hazardous-waste disposal unit.

aspects.label: Enzymes Contained
aspects.valueA: Hydrolytic enzymes (proteases, lipases, nucleases) active at acidic pH.
aspects.valueB: Oxidative enzymes, especially catalase, which breaks down hydrogen peroxide.

aspects.label: Main Function
aspects.valueA: Digests worn-out organelles, engulfed pathogens, and macromolecules.
aspects.valueB: Breaks down fatty acids (beta-oxidation) and detoxifies harmful peroxide byproducts.

aspects.label: Origin
aspects.valueA: Buds off from the Golgi apparatus.
aspects.valueB: Self-replicates by division, independent of the Golgi.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Lysosomes are called the 'suicide bags' of the cell because their enzymes can digest the cell itself if released.
overlay.memoryTrick: Peroxisome handles peroxide. Lysosome does lysis (breakdown).
overlay.commonMisconception: Peroxisomes don't digest whole organelles or pathogens like lysosomes do — their role is specific oxidative detox reactions.
